**3.5h**

October 6, 2026: Day 1 - Research, Feasibility & Component Selection

Key Learnings & Progress:

Understood how the ESP32-S3 serves as the main brain, running dual-core Wi-Fi/BLE processing alongside SPI and I2C peripherals.

Researched the CC1101 Sub-1GHz RF module to learn how it captures and transmits 315/433/868/915 MHz radio waves.

Designed the power architecture: USB Type-C ➔ TP4056 Battery Charger ➔ 3.3V LDO Voltage Regulator.

Decided on adding a 6-pin expansion header (UART/I2C) for future add-ons like GPS, I2S Microphones, or Speakers.
No physical PCB traces drawn yet, but gained 80%  clarity on component selection and schematic architecture.

October 7, 2026: Day 2 - Deep Dive into ESP32-S3 Pinouts & Module Workflows
Session Summary:

Dedicated today's session entirely to technical learning and understanding module compatibility via YouTube tutorials and technical documentation. Focus was placed on mapping out the ESP32-S3 architecture and making sure I don't accidentally assign peripheral functions to restricted or strapping pins.

Key Learnings & Progress:

Researched ESP32-S3 GPIO allocations: learned which pins are safe for general use, which are dedicated for flash/PSRAM, and which pins support native hardware SPI/I2C.

Studied power regulations and voltage requirements for individual modules (ensuring 3.3V tolerance on CC1101 and OLED).

Explored code upload workflows, USB-to-UART bridging versus Native USB flashing on the ESP32-S3, and basic firmware structure for driving the CC1101 transceiver.

No schematic drawing started in this session, but built the technical groundwork required before launching EasyEDA.

 Full EasyEDA Schematic Wiring & Electrical AuditingSession Summary:Worked continuously for over 2 hours on building the primary schematic for AeroDeck-3S in EasyEDA. Placed all major modules (ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, CC1101, MicroSD socket, TP4056, AMS1117, OLED screen, and 5-way navigation switch) and mapped out their pin-to-pin signal and power traces. Audited the full schematic to resolve critical wiring errors before moving to PCB routing.Key Progress & Technical Fixes:USB Type-C & Power Negotiation: Successfully wired the USB Type-C connector with $5.1\text{ k}\Omega$ pull-down resistors on CC1 and CC2 pins to enable standard C-to-C power delivery.   Power Rail Separation: Identified and separated the 5V VBUS rail from the 3.3V system power rail to prevent overvoltage damage to the ESP32-S3.   LDO & Charger Wiring: Fixed the AMS1117-3.3 pin mapping, routing OUT+ from TP4056 into VIN and deriving clean 3.3V from VOUT.   Bus Assignments: Corrected SPI lines for CC1101 and MicroSD card socket, and adjusted I2C pins (SDA $\to$ IO8, SCL $\to$ IO9) for the OLED screen.   Schematic layout is nearly complete and electrically audited. Next step: converting to 2-layer PCB layout!Time spent this session: 2 hours 3 minutes

### 2026-10-11 – Microcontroller Research & Selection

**1.18h**

Microcontroller Research & Selection
Limitations of ESP32-S3: Initially, the popular ESP32-S3 was considered, but it fell short of the advanced power efficiency, modern processor architecture, and cutting-edge wireless standards required for a dedicated handheld multi-protocol RF auditing device.

Budget & Optimization: The search focused on finding a chip that could deliver superior performance, low power consumption, and modern connectivity while strictly adhering to the $65 Hack Club budget.

Selecting the ESP32-C5-WROOM-1: Ultimately, the ESP32-C5 was chosen as the core microcontroller. Its modern RISC-V single-core architecture, native support for Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) and Bluetooth 5, and seamless compatibility with the sub-1GHz CC1101 module made it the ideal brain for the project.
